title: The La Vida Ballroom, dime-a-dance, and the drummer who slept
summary: He explains ten-cent dancing at the La Vida and the drummer who played steady tempo while sleeping.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yes, Celestin played mostly for ballrooms, colleges. Kid Rene' played this place called the La Vida Ballroom, it was 10¢ a dance place.

Well, the girls line up on one side of the room and they entice the men by doing a little sexy dance and turning around and pointing by their fingers for the men to come and dance with them. The music do not stop. The music starts about 8 o'clock. I remember by going to this job this one time and I never got out of that La Vida Ballroom until the summer was up, we played all night, and something phenomenal was happening around about midnight, you know, and we set a tempo and we stayed with that tempo and I'd turn around and since I just met the guys in the band, I'd look at the drummer and the drummer seems to be asleep. But you know, I couldn't hardly believe my eyes, this guy was fast asleep and playing at the same time with his eyes closed. I don't know if I can

convince you but this is the truth, this drummer was sitting up there, he set a tempo and then he'd go to sleep. We never varied the tempo at all. The music just never stops, and when you had to go to the bathroom, well, you had to take off one by one, you know.
The music couldn't shut down in other words.

No. No, because it was 10¢ a dance and the girls charged so much a dance and in the sequence of dances they try to get more and the customers that are lined up on the other side, why they get a great big roll of dance tickets and they go over and dance with the girls.
